root_cause.text: AppArmor's DFA unpacking code in security/apparmor/match.c directly cast arbitrary blob data to __be16/__be32 pointers and dereferenced them, assuming alignment for DFA tables that can come from kernel or userspace and may be unaligned.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces raw accesses like `*(__be16 *)(blob)`, `*(__be32 *)(blob + 8)`, and `ntohl(*(__be32 *) data)` in `unpack_table()` and `aa_dfa_unpack()` with `get_unaligned_be16()`/`get_unaligned_be32()`, while the CVE/commit explicitly states “8-byte alignment isn't always guaranteed” and shows `aa_dfa_unpack` triggering a “Kernel unaligned access” warning.

apparmor: fix restricted endian type warnings for dfa unpack

Signed-off-by: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit e6e8bf418850d7958311a96ccfb594f2bcc8313e
Author: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>
Date:   Mon Jan 16 00:43:13 2017 -0800

    apparmor: fix restricted endian type warnings for dfa unpack
    
    Signed-off-by: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>

diff --git a/security/apparmor/match.c b/security/apparmor/match.c
index 8f0806b35a75..eb0efef746f5 100644
--- a/security/apparmor/match.c
+++ b/security/apparmor/match.c
@@ -73,11 +73,11 @@ static struct table_header *unpack_
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact unpacking logic in the affected function(s). The vulnerable construct is still present: the code directly casts raw blob bytes to endian-typed pointers and dereferences them, e.g. `th.td_id = be16_to_cpu(*(__be16 *) (blob)) - 1;`, `th.td_flags = be16_to_cpu(*(__be16 *) (blob + 2));`, `th.td_lolen = be32_to_cpu(*(__be32 *) (blob + 8));`, and in `aa_dfa_unpack()` `if (ntohl(*(__be32 *) data) != YYTH_MAGIC)`, `hsize = ntohl(*(__be32 *) (data + 4));`, `dfa->flags = ntohs(*(__be16 *) (data + 12));`. The root cause says the bug is direct casting of arbitrary blob data to `__be16`/`__be32` pointers and dereferencing them while assuming alignment. That exact pattern exists here. This commit only changes casts from `u16/u32` to `__be16/__be32` and adjusts macro type arguments, which addresses endian type warnings, not unaligned access. There is no use of safe unaligned helpers such as `get_unaligned_be16()`/`get_unaligned_be32()` or equivalent bytewise extraction, so the fix is not present.

Author: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>
Date:   Thu Jul 29 14:48:01 2010 -0700

    AppArmor: dfa match engine
    
    A basic dfa matching engine based off the dfa engine in the Dragon
    Book.  It uses simple row comb compression with a check field.
    
    This allows AppArmor to do pattern matching in linear time, and also
    avoids stack issues that an nfa based engine may have.  The dfa
    engine uses a byte based comparison,
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet directly shows the unpacking logic and is sufficient to assess the root cause. In `unpack_table()`, the code reads fields from the serialized blob by casting `char *blob` to wider integer pointers and dereferencing them: `th.td_id = be16_to_cpu(*(u16 *) (blob)) - 1;`, `th.td_flags = be16_to_cpu(*(u16 *) (blob + 2));`, and `th.td_lolen = be32_to_cpu(*(u32 *) (blob + 8));`. In `aa_dfa_unpack()`, it likewise does `if (ntohl(*(u32 *) data) != YYTH_MAGIC)`, `hsize = ntohl(*(u32 *) (data + 4));`, and `dfa->flags = ntohs(*(u16 *) (data + 12));`. These are exactly the vulnerable constructs described: direct casts of arbitrary blob data to `u16 *`/`u32 *` and dereferences, which assume alignment. The function comment even says `@blob: aligned serialized stream of data to unpack` and `Assumes the dfa @blob stream has been aligned on a 8 byte boundry`, but the root cause is that DFA tables can originate from kernel or userspace and may be unaligned, so this assumption is unsafe. There is no use of safe unaligned access helpers such as `get_unaligned_be16()`/`get_unaligned_be32()`, nor any memcpy-based decoding, so the fix is not present.
